# SKWorld

> Sovereign AI infrastructure. An owned stack from silicon to soul: identity and
> post-quantum security, infrastructure, memory, communications, agents, and
> soul. 37 open projects across 7 layers, all running on hardware you control.

The thesis: every layer of an AI stack should be owned rather than rented. Your
data, your keys, your hardware. Adopting one piece never obliges you to adopt
the whole, and leaving is always possible.

## Three pillars

1. First principles. The default stack was not accepted. Every layer was
   questioned and rebuilt: open, swappable, yours.
2. The full vertical. No rented middle, no black-box bottom. One cohesive stack
   rather than a bag of services you depend on.
3. Data sovereignty. Your data is yours cryptographically and physically. It
   never leaves your control.

## Spotlights

The home page calls out three projects above the stack grid, in this order:

- SKPatch, patching at AI speed: https://skpatch.skworld.io/
- skaegis, continuous CVE detection (Detect in the Defend, Detect, Remediate
  suite with SKSec and SKPatch): https://skaegis.skworld.io/
- SKRSI, the evidence-first improvement loop that proposes and never
  authorizes: https://skrsi.skworld.io/

## Platform map and live status

The site also carries a platform map (every SKStacks service, grouped into
six layers: edge, identity, ops and patching, data, apps, comms/AI) and an
hourly-refreshed live status section for SKStacks, SKPatch and skaegis.

- Interactive platform map: https://skworld.io/diagrams/skworld.platform.html
- Platform map source (Archify JSON): https://skworld.io/diagrams/skworld.platform.json
- Live status snapshot (JSON, refreshed hourly): https://skworld.io/data/status.json
- SKPatch program: https://skpatch.skworld.io/
